report.answer_text:
On a typical horizontal-jib tower crane, the hoist moves the load up and down, the trolley moves it toward or away from the tower, and the slewing unit swings it around the tower. (morrow.com)
| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| Base and foundation | Support the crane and transfer its weight and overturning forces to the ground. (morrow.com) |
| Mast (tower) | The vertical steel structure that supports the upper assembly and gives the crane its height. (morrow.com) |
| Slewing unit (turntable) | Uses a large bearing and drive motors to rotate the upper assembly around the mast. (morrow.com) |
| Jib (working arm) | The long horizontal arm that supports the trolley and gives the crane its reach. (morrow.com) |
| Trolley | Travels along the jib, moving the suspended load closer to or farther from the mast. (morrow.com) |
| Hoist motor, drum, and wire rope | The motor turns the drum to wind or unwind the rope, raising or lowering the hook. (morrow.com) |
| Hook block | The hook-and-pulley assembly suspended from the hoist rope. The load attaches to the hook, usually through slings or other rigging. (morrow.com) |
| Counter-jib | The shorter arm opposite the working jib. It carries the counterweights and often the hoist machinery. (morrow.com) |
| Counterweights | Offset part of the overturning effect of the working jib and its load. (morrow.com) |
| Operator’s cab and controls | Let the operator control lifting, trolley travel, and rotation. Safety devices limit motions such as trolley travel and help prevent overloads. (morrow.com) |
A luffing-jib crane changes its reach by pivoting the jib up or down rather than moving a trolley along a horizontal arm. (govinfo.gov)
